value.first: Nights 1-3: keep the 3am waking as boring and dark as possible. When he wakes, wait a couple of minutes before going in. When you do go, keep it flat and brief - a hand on his back, a few quiet words, no picking up, no lights, no talking about it. Expect him to protest and maybe stand or cry harder the first two nights. That is normal and not you doing it wrong.
value.second: Nights 4-7: stretch the wait before you go in - try 5 minutes, then next time 10. Same flat response each time, then straight back out. If he only settles in your arms, put him down drowsy but awake so he practises the last step himself. Around now most toddlers start protesting less and resettling faster, though one bad night mid-week is common and not a reset.
value.third: After that: check the daytime edges too - an 18-month-old usually needs one nap ending by mid-afternoon and a wake window before bed, since an overtired or overtired-late toddler wakes at 3am. You'll know it's working when the waking shrinks or drops off within a week or two. If he's still fully waking every night after two weeks, or seems in pain when he does, worth raising with your doctor.
